notes: WMATA FY2018 Metro Performance Report ('up from 70 percent in FY17'), 'Rail Customer On-Time Performance' -- % of customer trips completed within expected wait+travel-time window, WMATA fiscal year (Jul-Jun), same metric/convention as the existing FY2025 real value already in this series. WMATA FY2018 Metro Performance Report (own annual report), same metric/convention as 2017.

WMATA Q4FY19 Metro Performance Report, same metric/convention as 2017. A later report's historical table lists this year at 85% instead -- treating 88% (from FY2019's own dedicated annual report) as primary since it's the closer-to-source figure.

WMATA FY2020 'Pre-Pandemic' Metro Performance Report -- this report explicitly covers only Jul 2019-Mar 15 2020 (pre-COVID), not the full fiscal year; the FY2022 Annual report's retrospective 3-year chart also shows 90% for FY20, suggesting this pre-pandemic figure was carried forward as the reported annual value with no distinct post-shutdown Q4 breakout found.

WMATA FY2022 Annual Metro Performance Report's 3-year retrospective chart, same metric/convention as 2017. Pandemic-era, very low ridership -- high OTP likely reflects light system loading, not necessarily improved operations.

WMATA FY2022 Annual Metro Performance Report, same metric/convention as 2017. Driven by the Oct 12 2021 WMATA 7000-series railcar wheelset/derailment safety crisis -- ~60% of the railcar fleet pulled from service, headways roughly doubled for months (quarterly breakdown: Q1 91%, Q2 71%, Q3 72%, Q4 81%). A real operational/safety event, not a metric-definition change.
WMATA FY2023/Q4 Metro Performance Report: 'An average of 90 percent of trips were completed on-time..., which was below the target of 92 percent.' Same metric/convention as 2017.
WMATA FY24 Annual Service Excellence Report, reconfirmed in the FY25 Annual Service Excellence Report. Same metric/convention as 2017.
